sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *por más que*, *por mucho que* and *por muy… que* from B2 Unit 8. They mean "no matter how much" and take the subjunctive when the amount is open. This lesson adds one small thing, *por más* or *por mucho* + noun + *que*, and compares these patterns with the relatives of this unit.

sections.title: New: a noun between por and que
rows: Por mucha prisa que tengas, no vas a llegar antes.
However much of a hurry you are in, you won't get there earlier.
Por más dinero que ahorres, ese viaje es caro.
However much money you save, that trip is expensive.
Por muchos años que pasen, no voy a olvidar este viaje.
However many years go by, I won't forget this trip.
Por más cansancio que sienta, voy a terminar hoy.
However tired I feel, I'm going to finish today.

sections.title: Agreement, and the difference from cualquiera que
sections.content: With *mucho* the noun decides the ending: *mucha prisa*, *muchos años*. *Más* never changes: *por más dinero*, *por más cosas*. These patterns answer the question "how much?": the amount makes no difference. *Cualquiera que* answers "which one?": the choice makes no difference. Both take the subjunctive.

items.spanish: Por mucha hambre que tengas, espera a los demás.
items.english: However hungry you are, wait for the others.

items.spanish: Cualquiera que sea el precio, voy a comprar el billete.
items.english: Whatever the price is, I'm going to buy the ticket.

items.spanish: Por más que ahorres, ese viaje sigue siendo caro.
items.english: However much you save, that trip is still expensive.

items.spanish: Por mucha prisa que tenía, llegó tarde.
items.english: However much of a hurry he was in, he arrived late. (It really happened: indicative.)

sections.content: As in B2 Unit 8, use the indicative when the effort or the amount really happened (*Por mucha prisa que tenía*), and the subjunctive when you look ahead or speak in general (*Por mucha prisa que tengas*).
